extracted.intended_audience: people wishing to contribute proofs or definitions to The Book of Statistical Proofs (mathematicians/statisticians with varying LaTeX/Markdown/GitHub skills)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for contributing theorems, proofs, or definitions to The Book of Statistical Proofs via three contribution levels: (1) suggest items, (2) submit formatted files, or (3) add pages directly via GitHub. Specifies required tools, templates, file placement, naming, metadata, and submission workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution levels (Level 1–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three different levels of contributing to the project, with contribution intensity increasing from Level 1 to Level 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level choice depends on your mathematical knowledge, computer skills, and time willingness. Quick-access links to repository, templates, wanted lists, and tools are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 1 — Suggest a theorem or definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Required: a web browser and access to Google Documents. Use the online document for suggesting a theorem or suggesting a definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter one proof source per row, following the instructions in the sheet. This level is for submitting pointers/sources rather than formatted proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 2 — Send a formatted file to the archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Required: LaTeX processing software and a Google Drive account. Pick a proof or definition and write it as a LaTeX document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optionally embed your submission into the provided Markdown templates for proof or definition. Submit your LaTeX or Markdown file via the online submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 3 — Add a page to the archive yourself via GitHub
rubrics_metrics.description: Required: Markdown processing software and a GitHub account. Fork the repository, add a page directly in the repository, and create a pull request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workflow: fork the repository; in subfolder P (proofs) or D (definitions) duplicate the file -temp-.md and rename it to [shortcut].md; rewrite the template into your proof/definition; fill metadata in the header; commit and launch a pull request (suggested subject: added "[shortcut]"). Your branch will be merged into master and go live after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming convention ([shortcut].md)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rename duplicated template -temp-.md to [shortcut].md where [shortcut] is an abbreviation of your proof (or definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise abbreviation as the filename; this becomes the page shortcut/identifier in the archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template usage and content rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate the provided template file (-temp-.md) and rewrite it to become a proof or definition of your theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the structure of the template when composing content; you may optionally embed LaTeX/Markdown content into the Markdown templates (templates for proof or definition are provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata header requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill in the metadata in the header of the document (enclosed by “---”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required metadata fields in the header are completed before committing; metadata drives indexing and display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository placement (P vs D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place new files in the appropriate repository subfolder: P for proofs or D for definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct placement ensures content is categorized properly in the archive and index pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Level-dependent submission methods: Level 1 via Google Sheets suggestion doc; Level 2 via online submission form; Level 3 via GitHub pull request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For GitHub PRs, use a clear subject (example: added "[shortcut]"). Optionally update index pages before committing. Follow the repository's PR workflow so your submission can be merged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional actions: embed into templates and update index pages
rubrics_metrics.description: You may optionally embed your LaTeX submission into the provided Markdown templates and/or update index pages before committing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding into templates helps uniform formatting; updating index pages helps navigation but is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and possible compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: When merged, your proof or definition will link to your GitHub profile. Additionally, you can earn money!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide notes that submissions link to contributor GitHub profiles and mentions the possibility to earn money, but provides no detailed payment criteria on this page.
